headline: The FBI sold him the rifle. Then it arrested him.
summary: An 18-year-old told an FBI informant he would kill non-Muslims at the Mall of America on October 24, in his words "maybe 30 to 60 people." Agents had watched him since December 2024. On Tuesday an undercover FBI employee sold him an AK-47 and 200 rounds for $600 in a park in Richfield, Minnesota, and arrested him on the spot.
cover_answer: No. Agents arrested him the moment he bought the gun.
table_question: Is it fair to catch someone by selling them what they asked for?

5-7.script: A young man in Minnesota said he wanted to hurt people at a very big mall. The police had been watching him for almost two years, the way a lifeguard watches one swimmer. When he tried to buy a gun, the seller was a police officer, and they arrested him right there. Nobody was hurt. The grown-ups have it.
5-7.why: Shielded. If it reaches them: the lifeguard was already watching, and the ending comes first.
5-7.why_long: Shielded: a seven-year-old can do nothing with a plan to kill, and takes one vivid feature for the whole event, so the script gives neither the number nor the target. The lifeguard is the anchor: an adult watching before anything went wrong. Expect "could it happen at our mall?" The FBI watched this one for two years.

8-12.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
8-12.script: An 18-year-old told someone online he would attack the Mall of America on October 24. That someone reported to the FBI, which had watched him for two years. When he went to buy a rifle, the seller was an agent: $600, an AK-47, arrested on the spot. A goalkeeper standing where the shot would go.
8-12.why: Messages, watching, the sale, the arrest, in order.
8-12.why_long: This age is working out cause and effect, so the script hands them the chain in order: messages to an informant, two years of watching, a sale that was a trap, an arrest. The goalkeeper was in place before the shot. Expect "isn't that a trick?" It is. The FBI says he picked the date and the target first.

13-17.script: If the FBI sells you the rifle, did it stop an attack or build one? An 18-year-old messaged an informant for two years, picked the Mall of America, paid an agent $600 for an AK-47. Arrested. Second: the FBI warned his parents in May 2025. His father sent them to a lawyer. What should yours do?
13-17.why: Sting or setup is theirs. Then the parents.
13-17.why_long: A teenager can hold two true things: the FBI watched a young man say for two years that he would kill, and the FBI put the rifle in his hands. Kuhn calls honest argument a skill they practise, so the script asks it straight, then turns to the parents who were warned. Expect "would you have let them in?" Say what you'd do.

5-7.a: No. The police arrested him the moment he tried to buy the gun. Nobody was hurt.

8-12.q: Why did the FBI sell him a gun?
8-12.a: So the gun was theirs, and they stood beside him as he took it.

8-12.q: How did they know about him?
8-12.a: He told someone online who reported to the FBI. Two years of watching.

13-17.q: Isn't selling him the rifle entrapment?
13-17.a: His lawyer hasn't said. The FBI says he chose the date and target himself.

13-17.q: Why didn't his parents stop him?
13-17.a: Agents went to the house in May 2025. His father sent them to a lawyer.
